Begin already rushing toward a massive black hole, its glowing accretion disk clearly visible ahead. The black hole initially occupies roughly one-third of the frame.

Accelerate continuously toward it. The dark circular shadow expands steadily as increasingly detailed ribbons of incandescent gas become visible within the disk. The space between the camera and the black hole remains clear, giving an uninterrupted view of the approaching darkness.

The camera banks slightly while continuing straight toward the same target. Light from the surrounding disk bends into smooth, connected arcs. The entire structure grows larger as the viewpoint draws dangerously close.

During the final three seconds, intensify the acceleration and subtle camera vibration. The black shadow expands until it dominates almost the entire image. The bright disk and its lensed arcs slide toward the edges of the frame as the camera closes in, maintaining a clearly defined dark center.

End with an abrupt cut to black at the moment of closest approach. Maintain continuous forward momentum throughout the shot.
